headline: All majors below 200-day lines with MACD diverging on alts; longs crowded and funded; whales moving BTC off exchanges into weakness.
paragraphs: The regime is in drawdown. All seven assets sit below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have achieved a golden cross. Bitcoin is 48.5 percent below its 12-month high; Ethereum 61.2 percent; Solana 70 percent; Dogecoin at a severe 75 percent. The entire cohort is in a bear regime by the strictest definition. What differs is the texture of that regime: Bitcoin's RSI sits at 50.2, straddling neutral, and its MACD is above signal line, suggesting the selling pressure has at least paused. Ethereum at 55.6 RSI and MACD positive shows similar equilibrium. But Solana's MACD is already below signal, RSI at 44.3, and Cardano's realized volatility is running at 70 percent, nearly double Bitcoin's 29.8 percent. The regime is not uniform; the smaller assets are rolling over inside a larger bear trend.

The momentum divergence is worth naming. Bitcoin and Ethereum are showing positive MACD and RSIs above the 40 line, yet both remain entrenched below their 200-day lines. Solana, XRP, and ADA show negative MACD, which aligns with the bear trend but breaks their recovery attempt. Dogecoin printed a 3.86 percent gain over 24 hours while sitting 75 percent below its yearly high, with MACD positive and RSI at 43.9. When a heavily drawdown asset rallies into negative momentum, it often signals capitulation buying or technician covering rather than a new trending move. The small caps are not following the large ones: Shiba up 17.5 percent, Avalanche up 8.68 percent, while UNI and World Coin are down 4 percent each. Breadth is negative even inside the rally.

Positioning tells a crowding story. Bitcoin open interest stands at 2.05 billion dollars with a long-to-short ratio of 1.73; Ethereum at 1.38 billion with a ratio of 1.86. These are longs in control, not by historic extremes, but materially skewed. Solana's ratio is 2.84, XRP at 3.22, and Dogecoin at 3.73, meaning three to four dollars long for every dollar short. Funding is still positive across the board: Bitcoin at 5.5 percent annualized, Ethereum at 3.7 percent, Dogecoin at 11 percent. When longs pay to hold and leverage is skewed, the system is funding the bias that profits from a downturn. Liquidations over the past 24 hours show 175 bitcoin longs versus 878 shorts cleared, and 358 ethereum liquidations split more evenly (489 K longs, 547 K shorts), suggesting longs are still intact but shorts are washing out. The boat is crowded on one side; the cost to stay there is rising.

Whale flows reveal conviction against spot buying. Over the past 72 hours, Bitcoin saw 77.5 million dollars net exit exchanges: 128.8 million withdrawn, 51.3 million deposited. The two largest moves off OKEx were 72 million and 56.8 million dollars. This is not panic liquidation; this is accumulation into weakness or hedging. The weekly trend shows volatility: two billion net inflow two weeks ago, then 577 million, then outflows of 147 and 146 million for the last two weeks. Whales are rotating. Stablecoin float sits at 306.9 billion dollars, down 1.59 percent over the month, which is modest supply decline. The traditional-finance bid is absent: Bitcoin ETF flows printed 240 million dollars outflow on July 24, Ethereum 70.7 million negative. The crowd is selling into spot instruments while large holders are moving coins into self-custody or cold storage. That asymmetry, not the direction itself, is the tell.

Sentiment is at 27, labeled Fear, in a 30-day range of 11 to 33, which means the crowd is genuinely scared and only slightly elevated from peak terror. Fear and Greed at the bottom of its recent band while assets hold above their 2-month lows and whales accumulate is a classic divergence: when retail sentiment reaches exhaustion and smart money is buying, the setup tends to hold. Market cap rose 0.41 percent even as spot flows turned negative, and Bitcoin dominance is stable at 56.5 percent. The tape is not screaming panic; it is showing resignation, which is a different condition.

Watch for two conditions to mark a shift. First, whether Bitcoin and Ethereum can reclaim the 200-day line without triggering fresh long liquidations. The crowd is heavy long and funded; a close above the 200-day would likely spike funding higher still and could shake out shorts, confirming the bias. Second, whether stablecoin float stabilizes or continues its slow drain. A reversal in whale net outflow, from moving coins off exchanges to moving them on, would signal the accumulation phase is complete and positioning is rotating forward. Bitcoin network fees are at 1 sat/vB and difficulty is preparing a slight downward retarget, neither sign of stress. The tape is not broken; it is tense, waiting for conviction on either side to show itself.
